title: GROUPOID: Groupoid-based aggregation for federated learning on Riemannian manifolds
description:
Pre-alpha research prototype exploring groupoid-based aggregation for federated learning on Riemannian manifolds. The supported point-valued aggregation path uses explicit invertible point actions, a cycle-basis holonomy defect diagnostic, the cellular sheaf Laplacian, and Karcher mean aggregation via geomstats. Tangent-vector parallel transport is provided separately through Schild and pole ladder utilities.

Scientific correction in v0.1.0.dev5: earlier releases described the cycle-basis holonomy statistic as a first-cohomology (H^1) norm. The implementation actually computes the maximum Frobenius deviation of holonomy from identity over the particular NetworkX cycle basis. Exact zero has a flatness interpretation under explicit connectedness, completeness, invertibility, reciprocal opposite-edge registration when both directions are supplied, and complete evaluation of every cycle emitted by the NetworkX cycle-basis routine (an argument specific to the NetworkX Paton implementation exercised here, not to arbitrary cycle bases), but the nonzero magnitude is basis-dependent and is not invariant under arbitrary invertible changes of frame. The stored preregistered benchmark values are unchanged; the historical H2 rho and permutation p-value are reinterpreted as statistics for this fixed cycle-basis defect, not for a canonical H^1 norm. This version also withdraws register_transport_from_points from the supported point-valued aggregation path: its ambient square operator is assembled from transported tangent vectors and does not generally define the invertible manifold point action that aggregation requires. Tangent-vector ladder validation remains supported. The ambient tangent-matrix helper is restricted to vector-shaped point representations. Direct registered matrices are supported only under the explicit point-action contract documented in the repository, including reciprocal opposite arrows when both orientations are stored. See CORRECTION_NOTICE.md for the full correction record.

The earlier v0.1.0.dev0 version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20563975 remains superseded and must not be cited for results. Exact historical versions should be cited by their version-specific DOI; project-level DOI metadata is maintained through the Zenodo version family.
